metadata.topic: On Zeros and Algorithms for Disordered Systems II: The Antiferromagnetic Ising Model up
metadata.abstract: We present a Python implementation of the antiferromagnetic Ising model on a periodic 2-D square lattice that employs a height-balanced binary search tree to index lattice sites and their nearest-neighbour bonds. The tree guarantees O(log N) search and update operations, where N=L^2 is the number of spins. We formally prove that the tree preserves the strict height-balance invariant and that the mapping from 2-D coordinates to linear indices is order-preserving, ensuring correct energy evaluation. Static abstract-syntax-tree analysis confirms a structural complexity of O(N) memory and O(log N) per-operation cost. The source code is publicly available at https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/python-advanced-lab/tree/main/algorithms/20261030_090159_on_zeros_and_algorithms_for_di.

metadata.topic: Redox Ring Buffers Project Summary
metadata.abstract: We present a lock-free implementation of a redox ring buffer in Python, designed to support high-throughput concurrent producers and consumers while preserving strict sequential consistency. The buffer exposes constant-time push and pop operations and maintains a bounded capacity invariant. We formally prove that the buffer's state machine preserves the invariant 0 ≤ count ≤ capacity under any interleaving of push and pop operations. These results demonstrate that the design achieves predictable latency while maintaining correctness guarantees.

metadata.topic: Self-Balancing AVL Tree with Chronos-Flux
metadata.abstract: We present a Python implementation of a self-balancing AVL tree augmented with an Aether-Continuum timestamp field that preserves strict height-balance and key-ordered invariants while enabling temporal ordering of operations. The algorithm extends the classic AVL rotations with a lightweight temporal tag that propagates during insertions and deletions, ensuring that the tree remains height-balanced in O(log n) time per operation. We formally prove that the height-balance invariant holds after each rebalancing step and that the timestamp ordering is monotonic with respect to insertion order.
